title: Provider requests now stop before a quota is exhausted, not after
items: CollegeFootballData, CollegeBasketballData, and The Odds API were all confirmed live at zero remaining calls for the current billing period, with nothing in this codebase tracking it -- roster talent and market comparisons were quietly degrading to "no data" across the live site with no record of why. Every one of those providers, and football-data.org and BallDontLie besides, already report the caller's exact remaining budget on every single response; this project simply never read it.

A new persisted ledger reads that number off every real response and refuses the next call before it fires once a provider's tracked budget hits a safety reserve, instead of firing blind and finding out via a 429. Verified end-to-end against the real, currently-exhausted CFBD API: the first call correctly recorded "0 remaining" from the live response, and an immediate second call was refused with zero network request made.

Coverage is automatic for CollegeFootballData, CollegeBasketballData, BallDontLie and API-Football -- any script building those adapters is protected with no code changes, including the existing backfill and talent-refresh tools. football-data.org and The Odds API are tagged individually since they route through a different, older fetch path.
